So 1982 TSR could employ more people for product design than WOTC can today? What does that say?

And no, I realize that 8 isn't all today:

>Sims confirmed that there are currently eight in-house full-time staff members, including the producer, remaining on the tabletop Dungeons & Dragons team, not including additional staff employed for art design, brand, and licensing.

But in 1982, there were more people involved than the 12 listed/pictured.

Examples: the adventure list (X6, Quag Keep), lists Tim Kilpin as Editor, Steve Peregrine as cover artist, Jeffrey Butler as Interior Artist, Ruth Hoyer as Graphic Designer, and maps by Diesel LaForce.

In the Article, Gary Gygax gives his OK to the project, Frank Mentzer recommends that the module be renamed, but also gives it an “Ok.” Others mentioned include Brian Blume, Will Niebling, Kevin Blume, and Harold Johnson.

So is WOTC on "life-support"?

Have you ever tried wolfram alpha? This search engine is doing exactly what you want.

I have and I agree, WA is great for scientific queries. However, I don't think there is a search engine which makes good use of semantic web. Perhaps if you are searching for well known figures (actors, politicians). Try searching for Voat on WA and you'll get results for an airport with no clear guide how to filter results. For example: it should ask me if Voat I am looking for was a person, an object, a country, a book, an article etc. Context is very important here and if a search engine can help the user define it - results could be signifficantly improved.

Perhaps your experience with WA hasn't met the expection yet, since it still in alpha stage, but I know WA was developed with the same purposes as your needs - a search engine to communicate with people, to answer your questions, to do your order using resouces from internet, not to just act as a index system to look up. That why Apple and BlackBerry and maybe some other vendors are using WA in their virtual assistance. Hope we won't have to wait too long for a real version of J.A.R.V.I.S.
